the ventilatory and metabolic responses of conscious rats to ambient hypoxemia or hypercapnia are increased during concomitant exposure to CO hypoxemia.
in rats, central hypoxic stimulation of respiration is not inhibited by the peripheral hypoxic stimulation that is associated with CO hypoxia.
the ventilatory and metabolic responses in rats exposed to hypoxia or hypoxia associated with hypercapnia are increased when they are exposed concomitantly to carbon monoxide hypoxia.

the study of the effects of ambient and central hypoxia on ventilatory and metabolic responses of conscious rats at different ambient temperatures.
the study of the ventilatory response to acute and chronic hypoxia in conscious rats.
the effects of ambient temperature on the responses of the ventilatory control system in rats exposed to ambient hypoxias and hypercapnias.

, in rats exposed to HxCO, the ventilatory responses of Hxam and hypercapnia are enhanced.
the carotid bodies are not essential for the control of ventilation during hypoxia and that the ventilatory responses of conscious rats to Hxam, HxCO, and CO2 are not depressed when VO2 is high.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ventilatory responses of rats to ambient hypoxias are not altered by carotid body removal.
the respiratory responses to hypoxia, hypercapnia, and cold are not independent but are influenced by each other.
the ventilatory responses of rats to HxCO are similar to their responses to HxCO2, suggesting that CO2 and CO act as respiratory stimulators via a common mechanism.
